newsitem.title: ITALY: Pavarotti says he'll keep singing till year 2001.
newsitem.headline: Pavarotti says he'll keep singing till year 2001.

text.p: Italian tenor superstar Luciano Pavarotti said on Wednesday he would carry on singing until the year 2001 -- and might not even retire then.
"I'll keep singing at least until the year 2001, which would be a 40-year career, and there's nothing to say I'll retire then," the 61-year-old opera star told Reuters.
He was speaking on the Mediterranean island of Capri at a ceremony to hand over $4.2 million raised through concerts and recordings to several children's charities.
A quarter of that was destined for one project, War Child, to build a music centre in the Bosnian town of Mostar.

Pavarotti said he was delighted to visit the romantic island of Capri, but kept tight-lipped about his own love life. He has left his wife of 35 years for his secretary Nicoletta Mantovani and some media reports have said he has secretly married her.
"I've never been to Capri in my life and I can see I've been missing something," Pavarotti said.
"For the moment I'm not getting married because obviously the divorce proceedings won't be complete for three years...In any case that's something that only concerns us."
